scenes.line1: Why do pages load faster the second time?
scenes.say: Why do websites load so much faster on your second visit? What’s happening behind the scenes?

scenes.label: Caching
scenes.sub: Stores files locally to skip repeat downloads.
scenes.say: Caching stores resources right in your browser, so you don’t re-download the same files every time.
Content Delivery Networks, or CDNs, serve assets from servers near the user. This means lower latency, faster loads, and more reliability.
Service workers run in the background. They intercept network requests and can serve cached responses, even offline.

scenes.question: Is long-term caching always best?
scenes.right: Long-term caching speeds up loads, but can serve stale files. Use cache busting with content hashes to update assets when needed.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: Is long-term caching always the best choice? Not always—sometimes it serves outdated files. Use cache busting to keep things fresh.
